title: Irena Sendler: Jars of Names
dek: The Polish social worker who helped smuggle children from the Warsaw ghetto — and hid their real names in jars.
mortality_event: Gestapo arrest, torture, and death sentence in 1943 before Żegota bribed a guard and she survived underground.
citation_passage: Irena Sendler (1910–2008) was a Polish social worker who helped rescue Jewish children from the Warsaw ghetto during the Holocaust. As head of the children's section of Żegota, the underground Council for Aid to Jews, she worked to move children into hiding and provide new identities. She kept coded records of their original names and placements so surviving relatives could find them after the war. The Gestapo arrested and tortured her in 1943 and sentenced her to death; Żegota rescued her before execution, and she continued working under another identity. This seven-page comic follows rescue, danger, and the preservation of children's identities within a wider network of help.
